- **[STANDING, non-recurring-effort — dated cycle-2026-07-15T0100] §3.3
  interaction rows — structural blocker, full reasoning below. Future
  cycles: cite this entry, do not re-derive.**

  **Row 1** (`interaction.human_bonus_feat_ability_bonus.pilot_pressure`,
  currently `Partial/ProductVisible`): blocked on its own documented
  condition — "generalize the named Human pilot pressure into the
  interaction-row model once a second computed interaction pressure
  exists." Precisely what would satisfy that condition: a compute-path
  branch in `pilot_compute.rs` where a **named non-Human race identity AND
  a named class identity jointly** determine a distinct derived value —
  not a race-row widening alone (those are class-blind by construction, see
  row 2 below) and not a class-row widening gated to Human alone (that is
  the *same* pressure this row already grounds, not a second one). None of
  the 32 §3.x cycles landed to date produces that combination. This is not
  claimed as structurally impossible the way row 2 is — a future
  interaction-row-shaped compute branch could in principle exist within the
  tranche's declared scope — but nothing in the corpus checked so far (7
  core races x 11 core classes, PF1 Core Rulebook only) has produced one,
  and none is expected to surface as a side effect of ordinary §3.1/§3.2
  widening cycles, since those are deliberately scoped to stay class-blind
  (race rows) or Human-gated (class rows) by the loop's own established
  idiom.

  **Row 2** (`interaction.non_human_any_class.progression_pressure`,
  currently `Unverified/Observed`): blocked on its own documented
  condition — "warranted only when a class row's compute path is proven to
  branch on a specific non-Human race identity." This cycle checked, by
  direct source read (not summary), every one of the 11 landed §3.2 class
  widenings' compute functions in `pilot_compute.rs`
  (`explain_barbarian_level1_chassis` L7482,
  `explain_bard_level1_spell_baseline` L11674,
  `explain_cleric_level1_spell_baseline` L10730,
  `explain_druid_level1_spell_baseline` L11219,
  `explain_fighter_class_features` L4363, `explain_monk_level1_chassis`
  L8063, `explain_hybrid_level1_chassis`+Paladin block L4853/L5066,
  `explain_ranger_level1_chassis_and_class_feature_separation` L5864,
  `explain_rogue_level1_chassis` L9019,
  `explain_sorcerer_level1_spell_baseline` L9518,
  `explain_wizard_level1_prepared_spell_baseline` L10290) plus a full-file
  grep for every race-identity reference
  (`grep -n "race_id\|Race::" src/rules_core/pilot_compute.rs`). Result:
  every one of these functions gates on `input.chosen.race_id !=
  HUMAN_RACE_ID { return; }` and nothing else — none contains an `else if`
  or any other branch keyed to a specific non-Human race id (Dwarf, Elf,
  Gnome, Half-Elf, Half-Orc, Halfling). The only other race-identity checks
  anywhere in the file live in the six non-Human race-seam functions
  themselves (`explain_dwarf_race_seam`, `explain_elf_race_seam`,
  `explain_gnome_race_seam`, `explain_half_elf_race_seam`,
  `explain_half_orc_race_seam`, `explain_halfling_race_seam`), and none of
  those six references `class_id` or any class identity at all — they fire
  identically regardless of chosen class. There is no third category of
  race-branching code in this file. This was independently corroborated by
  the operator's own statement that the PF1 Core Rulebook (as opposed to
  later splatbooks/supplements, which are explicitly out of this tranche's
  scope per the scope doc §0 premise and §5 non-goals — "no additional
  tomes beyond the Core Rulebook") has no race-gated class features at all
  — this cycle's direct code inspection is fully consistent with that
  claim, since every one of the 11 core classes' Core-Rulebook-verified
  level-1-through-12 features (independently checked against d20pfsrd and
  Archives of Nethys across the 32 prior landed cycles) applies uniformly
  regardless of race.

  **This makes row 2's blocker structural, not merely current.** No loop
  cycle bounded by this tranche's declared scope (7 core races, 11 core
  classes, Core Rulebook only, levels 1-20) can ever supply the
  race-branch row 2's own warrant condition requires, because that branch
  does not exist anywhere in the source material this tranche is scoped
  to consume. Row 2 can only become eligible via a future tranche-level
  scope decision that admits material containing a genuine race-gated
  class feature (e.g. a splatbook). It is not "still blocked, re-check
  next cycle" — it is "blocked until scope changes," a materially
  different and more final classification than every prior cycle's
  identical-looking "not eligible this cycle" note implied.

  **Neither row is closed or resolved.** Both remain genuine open §3.3
  acceptance criteria per the scope doc — row 1 sits at `Partial/ProductVisible`

equipment categories — structural blocker, dated cycle-2026-07-15T0400")
for the full reasoning. §3.5 only becomes eligible for a normal
cycle-level landing if a future tranche-level decision authorizes a
bounded equipment-reachability capability (e.g., a documented,
corpus-aware function signature added to `pilot_compute.rs` for the first
time, plus an explicit ruling on an item-id-to-corpus-record matching
convention) — watch for this specifically, it is the only event that can
reopen §3.5. Both §3.4 and §3.5 are now confirmed to share the identical
root cause (no corpus-aware compute path exists anywhere in
`pilot_compute.rs`; the SD18-PRELOOP composer's `ComposedCharacterInput`
is built and immediately discarded down to its `character_input` field at
every call site). Until a tranche-level decision addresses that shared
root cause, proceed to §3.2 level-13+ widenings or re-check §3.1's
remaining families (Elf weapon familiarity/bonus languages, Gnome
Hatred/Gnome Magic/weapon familiarity, Half-Elf Adaptability/Multitalented)
per the brief's priority order.

- **[STANDING, non-recurring-effort — dated cycle-2026-07-15T0400] §3.5
  equipment categories — structural blocker, full reasoning above. Future
  cycles: cite this entry, do not re-derive.**

  All 4 §3.5 category cards (`arms_armor`, `general`, `magic_items`,
  `equipmods`) are blocked on the same underlying gap, not on any
  category-specific issue. The corpus-side half of the acceptance
  criterion — "a representative sample of the category's items parse via
  SD17-B-5, land in `SourcePackageContent`" — is already proven,
  generically, for all 4 categories (real corpus verified live this cycle:
  `CORPUS_ROOT=/home/ubuntu/workspace/repos/pcgen/data cargo test --locked
  --test sd17_b5_equipment` → 21/21 green against the real
  `cr_equip_arms_armor.lst` / `cr_equip_general.lst` /
  `cr_equip_magic_items.lst` / `cr_equipmods.lst` files). Unlike §3.4,
  the consumer-side chosen-state surface also already exists:
  `CharacterInput.chosen.equipment_selections: Vec<EquipmentSelection>` is
  real, with `item_id`, `equipped_or_active`, and `active_state` fields
  (`src/rules_core/character_input.rs:23,50-71`). But the *link* between
  the two — "selectable from a chosen `CharacterInput`" actually resolving
  to a real corpus record, and "affect derived stats when equipped" — does
  not exist anywhere in the codebase: (1) `pilot_compute.rs`'s only
  equipment consumer, `require_active_state` (line 12842), matches an
  `item_id` against the chosen-state list alone and never touches a
  corpus; (2) every equipment-effect value in `pilot_compute.rs`
  (`CHAIN_SHIRT_ARMOR_BONUS`, `CHAIN_SHIRT_ARMOR_CHECK_PENALTY`,
  `WEAPON_FOCUS_TO_HIT_BONUS`, etc.) is a hardcoded literal baked into the
  GE-06 deterministic pilot fixture, not a value read from any
  `EquipmentRecord`; (3) no function in `pilot_compute.rs` accepts a
  corpus, `SourcePackageContent`, or `ComposedCharacterInput` parameter of
  any kind (confirmed via direct grep: zero matches for
  `corpus\|SourcePackageContent\|SourceContentRecord` outside comments);
  (4) the SD18-PRELOOP composer's own `ComposedCharacterInput` (which does
  carry both a `CharacterInput` and a `SourcePackageContent` together) is
  never consumed anywhere outside its own module's tests, and even its own
  round-trip proof test
  (`tests/sd18_preloop_consumer_compose.rs:217`) discards the `corpus`
  field before calling `compute_pilot_base_chassis`, passing only
  `composed.character_input`; and (5) no id-matching convention exists
  between `CharacterInput`'s `item_id` namespace (arbitrary strings like
  `"item:longsword"`) and the corpus's real PCGen equipment identity space
  (`EquipmentRecord.name`, e.g. `"Longsword"`, and its `KEY:` token) —
  inventing one would be a cross-cutting design decision affecting every
  future equipment cycle, not a bounded single-cycle change.

  **This makes §3.5's blocker structural, not merely current — the same
  classification as §3.4's.** Both spell schools and equipment categories
  are blocked on the identical root cause: `pilot_compute.rs` has no
  corpus-aware compute path anywhere, for any domain, and the composer
  that bridges chosen-state and corpus-state is deliberately
  derivation-free by its own documented contract ("no derivation, no rule
  evaluation... a transport-and-shape carrier," per
  `composed_input.rs`'s own module doc). Equipment's situation is
  genuinely *better* than spells' in one respect — the chosen-state
  selection surface (`equipment_selections`) already exists, so a future
  capability slice would not need to add a new `CharacterInput` field —
  but it is not eligible for a bounded loop cycle today, because the
  missing piece (a corpus-aware compute path, plus an id-matching
  convention with no established precedent anywhere in the codebase) is
  the same class of new-plumbing work the Hard Stops section reserves for
  tranche-level decisions, not cycle-level ones. No loop cycle bounded by
  "extend an existing seam function" can supply this without first
  building that plumbing from scratch.

  **Recommendation for future cycles:** stop re-deriving this analysis
  from scratch every cycle. A single line — "re-checked, still ineligible,
  see Open Blockers entry dated cycle-2026-07-15T0400 for the full
  reasoning" — is sufficient going forward, unless a future tranche-level
  decision explicitly authorizes a bounded equipment-reachability
  capability (a corpus-aware function signature in or adjacent to
  `pilot_compute.rs`, plus a ruling on the item-id-to-corpus-record
  matching convention). Until then, §3.4 and §3.5 both stay fully `open`;
  route to §3.2 level-13+ widenings or re-check §3.1's remaining families
  instead, per the brief's priority order. If a future tranche-level
  decision addresses the shared root cause for *either* §3.4 or §3.5, the
  same capability likely unblocks both — worth checking the other
  section's eligibility immediately if one reopens.

**Step 2 — is Wild Shape's uses-per-day already a grounded standalone
pillar anywhere in this codebase, the way Barbarian's rage-rounds-per-day
or Paladin's smites-per-day are?** Read every Druid Wild Shape comment in
`pilot_compute.rs` directly (lines ~2900-3120, ~13020-13070, ~13330-13450)
rather than trusting the progress doc's own prior summaries. Finding: at
every single prior level where the class table's Special column named a
Wild Shape frequency rise (4th "1/day", 6th "2/day", 8th "3/day", 10th
"4/day", 12th "5/day", 14th "6/day"), the codebase's own comments
explicitly and consistently declined to ground even the bare numeral,
using the same repeated reasoning each time: the frequency rise "is
bundled with a non-separable form-list expansion... and a functioning-level
upgrade... none of which are separable from the numeral without
misrepresenting the bundled feature as fully flat." No `wild_shape` /
`WildShape` / `WILD_SHAPE` identifier exists anywhere in
`src/rules_core/pilot_compute.rs` as an actual grounded constant or
computed record — every occurrence is inside a comment explaining why it
is deliberately NOT grounded. A repository-wide grep
(`grep -rn "wild_shape\|WildShape\|WILD_SHAPE" src/`, excluding
`pilot_compute.rs`) returned zero hits — no other file references it
either. `support_state_matrix.rs`'s own
`class.druid.progression_and_spell_burden` row text independently confirms
this from the matrix side: it lists "the animal-companion execution
burden, the Wild Shape execution burden, and the prepared divine spell
posture burden" as still-blocked burdens in its own `dimension` prose. By
contrast, `pilot_compute.rs:9136` (`rage_rounds_per_day = 4 +
constitution_modifier + 2 * (level_value - 1)`, exposed as
`class_chassis.barbarian.rage_rounds_per_day`) and `pilot_compute.rs:6242`
(`smite_evil_uses_per_day = 1 + (paladin_level - 1) / 3`, exposed as
`class_chassis.paladin.smite_evil_uses_per_day`) are both genuinely
standalone, freestanding integer records with no bundled shapeshifting/
form-list side effect — confirming the orchestrator's own analogy is
accurate for those two classes, and confirming by direct contrast that
Wild Shape has never been given the same treatment. **Conclusion: Wild
Shape's frequency-per-day has NEVER been grounded as a standalone pillar
in this codebase — landing it at level 16 would be the FIRST time,**
which the brief explicitly names as a case to NOT force.

fetched the actual "Wild Shape (Su)" ability-description prose (not just
the class table) from both d20pfsrd and `legacy.aonprd.com` independently.

beast shape N / elemental body N / plant shape N" upgrades stops at 12th
level ("at 12th level, a druid can use wild shape to change into a Huge
elemental or a Huge plant creature"); the 14th, 16th, 18th, and 20th level

prose at all — only the increased daily-use numeral. This means the

non-separable... functioning-level upgrade," extrapolated from the
level-4-through-12 pattern) does not actually hold for levels 14/16

rather than assumed by precedent. This is a real, checked finding, and it
means level 16's frequency rise is arguably MORE separable in principle

landing decision: the brief's decision rule is keyed on whether a Wild

**This cycle's task was the orchestrator-directed definitive investigation
of Bard's level-18 "Mass suggestion, versatile performance" row**, carried
forward unresolved across at least eight prior cycles' "Next cycle
instructions." Fetched Bard's levels 16-19 fresh from TWO independent
primary sources: a raw HTML parse of d20pfsrd.com's own class table (via
`curl` + a small Python tag-stripper, bypassing the AI-summarization
column-shift artifact the Sorcerer level-18 cycle's own investigation had
flagged) and the Archives of Nethys aonprd.com mirror via
`ClassDisplay.aspx` (WebFetch). Both agreed byte-for-byte: level 16 blank,
level 17 "Inspire courage +4, lore master 3/day", level 18 "Mass
suggestion, versatile performance" (BAB +13/+8/+3, Fort +6, Ref +11, Will
+11), level 19 "Inspire competence +6" — no misattribution, no source
disagreement, a third source was not required. Also fetched the actual PF1
rule text for Mass Suggestion, Suggestion, and Versatile Performance
directly rather than assuming from memory: Mass Suggestion's own text
reads "This ability functions just like suggestion, but allows a bard of
18th level or higher to make a suggestion simultaneously to any number of
creatures that he has already fascinated" — i.e. Mass Suggestion is not a
new mechanic, it is a strict widening of the 6th-level Suggestion
spell-like ability to a wider target set.

**Precedent investigation, and a correction to the orchestrator's own
framing.** The orchestrator's brief hypothesized that Sorcerer's Bloodline
Spell had been "treated 8 times" as "a flat, honestly-named, unproven
record with an explicit disclaimer" — implying a precedent existed for
grounding a spell/SLA-granting feature as a record with a disclaimer. A
direct read of `pilot_compute.rs`'s own Sorcerer bloodline-spell comments
(levels 3/5/7/9/11/13/15/17) found this framing was NOT accurate: at every
one of those eight levels, the bloodline-spell/bloodline-power text was
explicitly left OUT of any record at all — "both entries stay named by the
pre-existing `arcane_bond_and_bloodline_progression.unsupported`
diagnostic's ... language, unchanged" / "no new pillar record is added."
No Bloodline Spell record was ever created; the codebase's own
"named-but-unproven" idiom, used dozens of times throughout
`pilot_compute.rs` (Wizard's open-ended Bonus Feat, Dirge of Doom, Inspire
Greatness, and Bard's own 6th-level Suggestion among them), consistently
means the ABSENCE of any record — not the presence of a disclaimed one.
This is distinct from the codebase's separate "bounded grant-only identity
record" idiom (Ranger's Endurance, Bard's own Soothing Performance/
Jack-of-All-Trades/Lore Master), which DOES emit a flat record for
automatic, non-spell class features with no player choice and no spell/SLA
content. The dividing line the codebase has already drawn, confirmed by
reading every relevant precedent directly rather than trusting the brief's
paraphrase: features that grant access to CAST OR USE A SPELL OR
SPELL-LIKE ABILITY (bloodline spells, New Arcana, Suggestion) get NO
record at all, ever — while non-spell binary trait grants (a feat, a
performance option, an identity) get a bounded grant-only identity record.
The directly on-point precedent for Mass Suggestion is therefore NOT the
Sorcerer bloodline-spell idiom (which the brief mischaracterized) but the
Bard's own 6th-level Suggestion precedent
(`tests/sd13_bard_level6_progression.rs`,
`bard_level6_does_not_fabricate_suggestion_or_versatile_performance`),
already on the books in this exact class row: "Suggestion is a spell-like
ability requiring a fascinated-target prerequisite and the 'suggestion'
spell's own effect-resolution engine (neither exists in this codebase) ...
so no new pillar record is grounded." Since Mass Suggestion is explicitly,
by its own rule text, the identical mechanic widened to more targets, it
inherits the identical blocker and is, if anything, further from
groundable (an added multi-target dimension) rather than closer.
"Versatile performance" was independently confirmed to be the same
already-declined choice-gated skill-substitution engine repeating for a
fifth time (levels 2/6/10/14/18, "every 4 levels thereafter" per its own
rule text).
